title: Add guided Omawake and Omaspeak setup
head: 69dcf6fe74a1
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: Failed/interrupted guided setup makes Install > AI unselectable once the package was added
leads.consequence: If guided setup is cancelled/invalid or check fails after omarchy-pkg-add succeeds, the app is installed but not ready and the menu immediately treats it as installed and disables guided setup. A user cannot retry via the Install menu and must know the CLI or remove and reinstall. The same applies if service enablement fails after configuration. Keep the install action available until actual setup/service state is ready, or offer a repair/configure action.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus F2; published as finding 2

leads.summary: Both removers leave the desktop setup launchers behind
leads.consequence: Successful guided setup installs ~/.local/share/applications/{omawake,omaspeak}-settings.desktop, which neither remover calls setup menu --uninstall nor deletes. After dropping each package, the Applications launcher still advertises an executable removed from /usr/bin; after reinstall, it can be stale if setup does not complete. Clean the app-owned launcher before dropping the executable, accounting for XDG_DATA_HOME.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus F1; published as finding 1

leads.summary: Remove ignores relocated XDG homes and leaves model/config/user unit data
leads.consequence: Both apps resolve XDG_CONFIG_HOME, XDG_DATA_HOME, XDG_CACHE_HOME and XDG_STATE_HOME if set; their setup writes there. Removers only delete HOME defaults and still announce all local data removed, leaving relocated models, configuration, cache, and state. setup systemd --uninstall removes the relocated user unit, but does not remove the relocated other four directories. Use resolved XDG paths with safety validation and the exact app subdirectory.
leads.triage: XDG overrides: Opus noted as minor, Omarchy does not set them; dropped

leads.summary: An app-managed unit can remain enabled/running despite a successful remover notification
leads.consequence: The upstream uninstall deliberately ignores systemctl --user disable --now failure; then either removal or daemon-reload can fail. The wrappers ignore even the resulting non-zero uninstall status, drop the package, delete data and report success. With a failing/unavailable user systemd manager an enabled or running unit can survive, potentially retrying an executable that was removed. Do not announce success or drop the package before verifying service teardown, or surface actionable failure and safely defer cleanup.
leads.triage: upstream uninstall ignores disable failure; packaging ALPM PreTransaction hook stops units on package removal (Opus Q2); low value, dropped

leads.summary: Package-absence shortcut strands app state and removes the recovery menu item
leads.consequence: If the package was removed directly, or if pacman -Q fails because the package database cannot be queried, both removers say not installed and skip uninstalling the user unit, launcher and local data. The Remove menu also hides the recovery route. The unit lives in the user's XDG config independent of package ownership and may remain enabled. Check unit/data independently of the package before skipping cleanup.
leads.triage: package-absent shortcut; same pattern as existing removers, ALPM hook handles units; dropped

leads.summary: Running removal with sudo operates on root's home and user manager, not the invoking desktop account
leads.consequence: Both scripts advertise requires-sudo and lack a desktop-user guard. Invoking the CLI through sudo changes HOME/user context: upstream setup systemd --uninstall targets the wrong user's unit; ~ cleanup targets the wrong home, but omarchy-pkg-drop removes the shared package. Original user's service and models/config survive and the script reports success. Refuse root invocation or resolve the invoking account in both service and cleanup steps; ordinary menu invocation is nonroot.
leads.triage: sudo removal targets root home; Opus notes same as existing removers and #9571; pre-existing pattern, dropped

leads.summary: Cancelling an app's interactive setup can still start its service when a prior configuration passes check
leads.consequence: At packaged versions each setup returns success on the user's Cancel choice, with no changes. On a previously configured system where setup check passes, the wrapper then runs setup systemd, enabling/restarting the service and sending Ready despite the user's explicit cancellation. A failed earlier install or manual package install makes this reachable. Consider distinguishing cancellation from successful guided apply rather than treating any zero exit as consent to activate.
leads.triage: cancel with prior valid config proceeds; Opus judged acceptable (user confirmed enablement); dropped

leads.summary: The added failure-path tests would still pass if package installation errors were ignored
leads.consequence: The package-add stub always exits zero and the test only forces setup and check failures. A mutation to `omarchy-pkg-add omawake-bin || true` passes every new test, so an installer could enter setup after the package transaction failed without being caught. Add an adjustable nonzero package-add stub and assert no setup, service activation or ready notification on that path for both commands.
leads.triage: factual: surviving mutant pkg-add || true; coordinator read Sol receipt (status 0) and Opus self-check reran it (RC, both apps 0); published as optional note

leads.summary: Both AI menu submenus lose their alphabetical order with the new items
leads.consequence: Source-order rendering places Omawake and Omaspeak before Grok and Hermes, even though the other AI entries are alphabetically ordered; within the new pair Omaspeak should precede Omawake. Move them after Ollama, before OpenClaw, Omaspeak then Omawake, in both menus. Lower priority cosmetic issue.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus F3 (nit); published as optional note scoped to Install > AI

limits: No real user manager, package database or desktop was touched; launcher and systemd consequences were verified from pinned upstream v0.0.2/v0.0.1 source, not from a live machine.
Menu visual appearance was not observed; order derives from JSONC and MenuModel source.

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** The removers leave the setup launcher behind, and a failed setup cannot be resumed from the menu.

### Removers leave the setup launcher behind

Full guided setup writes `~/.local/share/applications/<app>-settings.desktop` (upstream `src/setup/menu.rs`). The removers delete only the data directories, so it survives, pointing at the removed binary.

**Suggested change:** add the launcher to the `rm -rf` line (or run `<app> setup menu --uninstall || true` before the drop).

<details><summary>Reproducer (fails at 69dcf6f)</summary>

Save as `test/shell.d/oma-ai-remove-launcher-test.sh` in the PR checkout and run `bash test/shell.d/oma-ai-remove-launcher-test.sh`.

```bash
#!/bin/bash

set -euo pipefail

source "$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/base-test.sh"

tmp_dir=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$tmp_dir"' EXIT

mkdir -p "$tmp_dir/bin" "$tmp_dir/home"
export HOME="$tmp_dir/home"
export PATH="$tmp_dir/bin:$PATH"

for stub in omarchy-pkg-present omarchy-pkg-drop omarchy-notification-send omawake omaspeak; do
  printf '#!/bin/bash\nexit 0\n' >"$tmp_dir/bin/$stub"
  chmod +x "$tmp_dir/bin/$stub"
done

for app in omawake omaspeak; do
  # Guided "Full setup" writes this launcher (upstream src/setup/menu.rs, launcher_path).
  launcher="$HOME/.local/share/applications/$app-settings.desktop"
  mkdir -p "${launcher%/*}"
  printf '[Desktop Entry]\nExec="/usr/bin/%s" setup\n' "$app" >"$launcher"

  "$ROOT/bin/omarchy-remove-ai-$app" >/dev/null

  [[ ! -e $launcher ]] ||
    fail "$app removal deletes the launcher its guided setup installed" "left behind: ${launcher#"$HOME"/}"
  pass "$app removal deletes the launcher its guided setup installed"
done
```

Output at the reviewed head (69dcf6fe), exit status 1:

```
left behind: .local/share/applications/omawake-settings.desktop
not ok - omawake removal deletes the launcher its guided setup installed
```

The same output and status were recorded with the PR merged onto quattro 8b4eae66. Adding `~/.local/share/applications/<app>-settings.desktop` to each remover's `rm -rf` line makes this test pass for both apps, and the PR's own test still passes.
</details>

### Failed setup is a dead end from the menu

The package is added before `setup`. On a fresh install a cancelled setup exits 0, then `setup check` fails (no model yet). The Install row is `disabled` once the package is present, so it cannot be picked again, and nothing points back to the installer.

**Suggested change:** on failure, print that re-running `omarchy-install-ai-<app>` finishes setup.

<details><summary>Reproducer (fails at 69dcf6f)</summary>

Save as `test/shell.d/oma-ai-install-retry-test.sh` in the PR checkout and run `bash test/shell.d/oma-ai-install-retry-test.sh`.

```bash
#!/bin/bash

set -euo pipefail

source "$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/base-test.sh"

tmp_dir=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$tmp_dir"' EXIT

mkdir -p "$tmp_dir/bin" "$tmp_dir/home"
export HOME="$tmp_dir/home"
export TEST_LOG="$tmp_dir/log"
export PATH="$tmp_dir/bin:$PATH"

for stub in gum omarchy-pkg-add omarchy-pkg-drop omarchy-notification-send; do
  printf '#!/bin/bash\nprintf "%%s %%s\\n" "$(basename "$0")" "$*" >>"$TEST_LOG"\n' >"$tmp_dir/bin/$stub"
  chmod +x "$tmp_dir/bin/$stub"
done

# Upstream guided setup prints "Setup cancelled." and exits 0 when the user
# backs out; setup check then fails because no model was installed.
cat >"$tmp_dir/bin/omawake" <<'STUB'
#!/bin/bash
printf 'omawake %s\n' "$*" >>"$TEST_LOG"
[[ $* == "setup" ]] && echo "Setup cancelled."
[[ $* == "setup check" ]] && exit 1
exit 0
STUB
chmod +x "$tmp_dir/bin/omawake"

if output=$("$ROOT/bin/omarchy-install-ai-omawake" 2>&1); then
  fail "omawake install stops when guided setup is cancelled"
fi
grep -qx 'omarchy-pkg-add omawake-bin' "$TEST_LOG" && ! grep -q '^omarchy-pkg-drop' "$TEST_LOG" ||
  fail "omawake stays installed after a cancelled setup" "$(cat "$TEST_LOG")"
pass "omawake stays installed after a cancelled setup"

run_node_test <<'JS'
const fs = require('fs')
const menu = requireFromRoot('shell/plugins/menu/MenuModel.js')
const items = Object.fromEntries(menu.parseMenuJsonc(fs.readFileSync(path.join(root, 'default/omarchy/omarchy-menu.jsonc'), 'utf8')).map(item => [item.id, item]))
const row = items['install.ai.omawake']
assert(menu.isDisabled({ 'install.ai.omawake': true }, row), 'Install > AI > Omawake cannot be picked again once omawake-bin is present')
JS

[[ $output == *omarchy-install-ai-omawake* ]] ||
  fail "omawake install says how to finish setup once its Install row is dimmed" "$output"
pass "omawake install says how to finish setup once its Install row is dimmed"
```

Output at the reviewed head (69dcf6fe), exit status 1:

```
ok - omawake stays installed after a cancelled setup
ok - Install > AI > Omawake cannot be picked again once omawake-bin is present
Setup cancelled.
not ok - omawake install says how to finish setup once its Install row is dimmed
```

The same output and status were recorded with the PR merged onto quattro 8b4eae66. With the installer printing a next step when setup, check or service install fails, all three assertions pass and the PR's own test still passes.
</details>

<details><summary>Details</summary>

**Verified**
- Every failure path (gum declined, `omarchy-pkg-add`, `setup`, `setup check`, `setup systemd`) stops before the "Ready" notification; `setup check` and `setup systemd` exist with the relied-on exit codes in the upstream source.
- `omawake-bin` and `omaspeak-bin` are published on stable, rc and edge for x86_64 and aarch64.
- `test/shell.d/oma-ai-install-test.sh`, `menu-test.sh`, `menu-guards-test.sh` and `bin-style-test.sh` pass at the head and with the PR merged onto current `quattro`.

**Optional notes**
- The new test still passes when the installer ignores a failed package install (`omarchy-pkg-add omawake-bin || true`); a case where the `omarchy-pkg-add` stub fails would catch that.
- Omawake and Omaspeak are inserted between Dictation and Grok Bot, breaking the alphabetical order of Install > AI; Omaspeak then Omawake, between Ollama and OpenClaw, keeps it.
</details>
